title: Atlas Evaluation
description: One evaluation, embedded in the `evaluations` array of an atlas-run.v1 document.

missing_sections.description: Machine-readable section codes the executor can close on a retry.

should_retry.description: True only when an actionable gap remains and the iteration budget allows another pass.

evidence_gaps.description: Machine-readable evidence gap codes. Separate from missing_sections: a heading being present says nothing about whether the claim under it is supported. The last three codes come from deterministic checking and only occur on a run that carried an evidence base; the enum was widened additively, so documents written against the earlier code set still validate.

unverified_claims.description: Findings that are not supported: on the citation-only path, findings naming no observed source; on the deterministic path, findings with no machine-readable citation or whose citation did not survive checking. Hypotheses, not findings.

evidence_coverage.description: Share of findings that name an observed source. Null when the route has no evidence contract, or when the output asserts no finding. Citation only: a covered finding names a source that was read, it is not checked against that source's contents.

citation_checks.description: Per-finding result of deterministic checking, so a score can be followed back to a source. Empty on a run with no evidence base. `citations_are_sound` is about the pointer; `claim_check` is about what the finding declared. A verdict of `verified` or `contradicted` comes only from a typed claim, where the claim is the predicate; a settled free condition never produces one.

verification_method.description: semantic means a declared condition was settled against the source. Anything else means the claim itself was not checked.

claim_check.description: The outcome of settling what the finding declared about itself. Null when the route requires no claim check, or when the citations were unsound — a refutation resting on a source the finding cannot point at would be an accusation about the wrong file, so unsound citations never reach this step.

result.description: verified/contradicted come only from a typed claim, where the claim is the predicate. condition_supported/condition_refuted come from a producer's own free-standing test and say that the test passed or failed — not that the claim holds or fails.

is_decisive.description: Whether this result may move the finding's verdict. True only for verified and contradicted.

checked.description: What was evaluated, including the line range it was settled over, so a reader can see the scope.

retry_is_possible.description: Whether anything remained that another pass could act on, ignoring the iteration budget. With `should_retry`, which folds the budget in, this says whether the bound stopped the run or whether there was nothing left to try.

blocked_by.description: Evidence failures no re-wording can repair, as atlas-finding status codes. Non-empty means the sources must be observed again; the run then stops `blocked` rather than reporting a verdict on the answer.
